title: The Torah's garments (Zohar 3:152a)
hookLine: the stories are the Torah's clothing; look for the soul inside
last: WHERE COMPANIONS TALK TORAH, THE PRESENCE WALKS ALONG.

cards: A person walks down the street in a beautiful coat. Many passersby see only the coat. A few notice the person wearing it: how they walk, the look on their face.
Fewer still wonder what that person is like inside, what they love, what keeps them up at night. The Zohar takes that ordinary street and turns it into a way of reading.
Its sages say the Torah walks among us dressed, too. And they ask a sharp question about what we've been looking at all along.

teach.b: The Torah's garments. The passage sits in the Zohar's section on the book of Numbers, and it opens with something close to a dare.
If the Torah were only stories about ordinary people, it says, we could write a book like that ourselves, perhaps even a finer one. So the stories must be more than they look. First, the garment.
The Zohar says the tales of the Torah are its clothing. Abraham bargaining, Jacob wrestling, a donkey that speaks. They're real and worth reading, and they're also what the Torah is wearing.
Under the garment, the Zohar says, is the body of the Torah, and it names the commandments as that body: the shape the Torah takes in a life. Third, the soul.
Inside the body is the soul, the innermost Torah, and the passage says the wise, the ones who stood at Sinai, look only there. Fourth, the people looking.
The Zohar sorts readers like passersby on the street. Some see only the clothing, and stop. Some see the body under it.
And some look through both to the soul. Notice what the passage doesn't do. It doesn't throw the garment away.
Clothing is how a body moves among people; without it, nobody would meet the Torah at all. The Zohar's complaint is only with the reader who thinks the coat is the whole person. So the stories stay.
They're the doorway, not the whole house.

how: This Zohar passage is taught in Jewish study as a way of reading Torah on more than one level, and the plain sense of the story is still learned first, with deeper readings built on top of it.

o: the Torah's stories as clothing over its body and soul
the cloth covers that dress a Torah scroll
the robes the priests wore to serve in the Temple

games.q: the Torah, dressed — tap the pairs.

s: the Zohar says the Torah's stories can be thrown away
it calls them the garment: the way anyone meets the Torah at all.
the passage says people could write a finer book of ordinary stories
if the Torah were only stories, it says, we could write one ourselves, so there must be more.
in the passage, the commandments are the Torah's clothing

games.q: you meet the Torah on the street, dressed in its stories. according to the Zohar, where do the wise look?
o: at the garment, the stories alone.
at the body, and stop there.
games.why: the wise, the passage says, look at the soul, the innermost Torah, and the garment still stays on.

practice: Choose one ordinary thing near you, a cup, a coat on a hook, a photo, and look at its surface: its color, its shape, how it sits.

Then go one layer down, who made it and what it's for, and if you like, one more: what it carries for you or someone you love. No need to find anything grand; just keep going under, gently, one layer at a time.

wordCard.voice: The Torah's garments. The Zohar's picture: the stories are the Torah's clothing, the commandments its body, and inside, a soul for those who look. Today's words.

orig.note: Hebrew: a garment, clothing. The Zohar itself is written mostly in Aramaic.

carryVoice: Your line: look beneath the garment. A coat is never the whole person. I'll be here tomorrow.
